issues.legal_issue: A respondent whose decree is entirely favorable is not required to appeal or file cross-objections solely to contest an adverse finding and may challenge that finding while supporting the decree in the appellant’s appeal.
material_facts: The trial court dismissed the first and second suits in their entirety, but made findings adverse to the State on whether the disputed land formed part of government land.
The plaintiffs appealed the dismissal decrees, and the State sought to dispute the adverse findings in those appeals.
issues.conclusion: The State was not obliged to appeal or file cross-objections to challenge the findings while supporting the decrees dismissing the suits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(2) and 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an appeal lies against a decree, not a mere finding. Order XLI Rule 22, as amended, permits a respondent to file cross-objections against an adverse finding, but a respondent whose decree is entirely favorable may support it without cross-objections. Order XLI Rule 33 also empowers the appellate court to make an appropriate order. The Court applied Banarsi v. Ram Phal and Hardevinder Singh v. Paramjit Singh, and referred to Sri Nazeer Ahmed v. State Bank of Mysore.

rule.if: appeal_against_dismissal_decree and decree_entirely_favors_respondent and adverse_finding_against_respondent and respondent_seeks_to_support_decree

predicates.appeal_against_dismissal_decree: A plaintiff appeals a decree dismissing the plaintiff’s suit.
predicates.decree_entirely_favors_respondent: The decree grants the respondent all the relief available under it.
predicates.adverse_finding_against_respondent: The trial court records a finding on an issue against the respondent despite granting a wholly favorable decree.
predicates.respondent_seeks_to_support_decree: The respondent seeks to uphold the decree in the plaintiff’s appeal.
predicates.respondent_may_challenge_adverse_finding: The respondent may contest the adverse finding without filing cross-objections when doing so to support the favorable decree.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff appeals a wholly favorable dismissal decree, the respondent may contest an adverse finding without cross-objections in order to support that decree.

issues.legal_issue: An adverse finding in a suit does not operate as res judicata in a related appeal when the decree in that suit remains under appeal and the finding has not attained finality.
material_facts: Three suits concerning competing claims to land were tried together, with common evidence recorded.
The first and second suits were dismissed, and the plaintiffs appealed those decrees.
The State appealed the decree in the third suit, and the findings in the first and second suits remained subject to the pending appeals.
The State’s position that the land formed part of government land had been rejected in findings in the first and second suits.
issues.conclusion: The findings in the first and second suits did not operate as res judicata in the appeal concerning the third suit because the decrees and findings in the first and second suits had not attained finality.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, read with Explanation I, applies to a matter directly and substantially in issue in a former suit that has been heard and finally decided. A decree that remains under appeal has not attained the finality required for the adverse finding to bind the parties as res judicata in the related proceeding. The Court distinguished Sheodan Singh v. Daryao Kunwar and Lonankutty v. Thomman, where the relevant decree had become final, and considered Narhari v. Shankar and Sri Gangai Vinayagar Temple v. Meenakshi Ammal.

rule.if: appeal_in_related_suit and issue_decided_in_related_suit and decree_in_that_suit_remains_under_appeal and finding_has_not_attained_finality

predicates.appeal_in_related_suit: A court is hearing an appeal concerning one suit among related suits.
predicates.issue_decided_in_related_suit: The same issue was decided in another related suit.
predicates.decree_in_that_suit_remains_under_appeal: A party has appealed the decree in the related suit, leaving it pending appellate determination.
predicates.finding_has_not_attained_finality: The finding remains open to review in the pending appeal.
predicates.finding_does_not_operate_as_res_judicata: The finding does not bar consideration of the issue as res judicata in the related appeal.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning a related suit, a finding in another suit whose decree remains under appeal and whose finding is not final does not operate as res judicata.
